papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting long-term progression of Alzheimer's disease using a multimodal deep learning model incorporating interaction effects (Wang et al., J Transl Med 2024)
Predicting Progression from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease using MRI-based Cortical Features and a Two-State Markov Model (Ficiara et al., ISBI 2021)

what_each_reports.P-273: DISFC trimodal model (3D sMRI + 14 demographic/neuropsychological features + 49 SNPs), 238 ADNI-1/GO/2 MCI, conversion within 48 months, 10-fold CV: AUC 0.962 (SD 0.041); ADNI-3 test n=14 AUC 0.939.
what_each_reports.P-198: Two-state Markov model with five FreeSurfer cortical-thickness covariates feeding a logistic regression, 721 ADNI1/2 MCI (188 converters), conversion by the second visit about two years later, stratified 10-fold CV: AUC 0.78 +/- 0.08 (sulcal width 0.71 +/- 0.09; no covariates 0.56 +/- 0.10).

quantity_a: ROC-AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion within 48 months, ADNI, predictors = sMRI + cognitive/clinical scores + SNPs, 10-fold CV
quantity_b: ROC-AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion within ~2 years, ADNI, predictors = five MRI cortical-thickness measures only, 10-fold CV
incompatible_if_same: No: a trimodal model with cognitive scores and genotypes outscoring a five-covariate MRI-only Markov/logistic model is expected and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match in label (T2) but horizon differs: 48 months vs ~24 months.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (ADNI-1/GO/2 vs ADNI1/2; overlapping participants likely).
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal 10-fold CV for the quoted figures.
gates.modality_family: mismatch in predictor set: P-273 MRI + neuropsychological scores + SNPs; P-198 structural MRI cortical thickness only.

endpoint_and_metric: partly compatible: both ROC-AUC, but horizons differ (4 years vs 2 years) and predictor sets differ.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.962 is below 0.97; an (n=14) independent test exists; not a like-for-like performance comparison in any case.
independence: Distinct groups (Shanghai Jiao Tong vs Turin/USC); both use ADNI MCI participants, so cohort overlap is likely (non-independence).
grounds: P-273's 0.962 depends on cognitive test scores and genotypes as well as MRI, whereas P-198's 0.78 uses five MRI cortical-thickness covariates only.
P-273 predicts conversion within 48 months; P-198 predicts transition by a second visit about two years after baseline.
With predictor set and horizon both different and no waiver on record, the two AUCs are not the same quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: On the cross-validation set, our model achieved superior results for predicting MCI conversion within 4 years (AUC, 0.962; accuracy, 92.92%; sensitivity, 88.89%; specificity, 95.33%)
For each participant, we considered 14 clinical features at baseline, including demographic data (age, sex, education) and cognitive assessments
using λ to predict whether a test patient will transition to AD within the next two years, given the outcome of the first visit.
cortical thickness (AUC=0.78 ± 0.08; Accuracy= 0.75 ± 0.02) compared to the baseline model (AUC=0.56 ± 0.10; Accuracy=0.65 ± 0.08).

record_defects: resolution_note 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (AUC); Gap magnitude 0.182 exceeds threshold' ignores the 4-year vs 2-year horizon and trimodal vs MRI-only predictor sets.
resolution 'Rejected - false positive', resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' and the note's 'Confirmed genuine' contradict each other.
P-198 registry Best_Metric 'AUC 0.56' is the no-covariate baseline, not the best model (0.78).
The record classifies the pair as structural_mri for both, but P-273's quoted AUC rests on clinical and genetic inputs too.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-273 MRI-only AUC at a two-year horizon (not reported) set against P-198's 0.78 with non-overlapping uncertainty.
